definitions.terms: In every test: a letter is any Unicode letter of any script; a digit is any Unicode number character, so a fraction sign or a superscript figure counts; whitespace is what the JavaScript class \s matches; to trim is to remove whitespace at both ends; uppercase means the Unicode uppercase letters; a Hebrew character is any character from U+0590 to U+05FF, letters, points, maqaf and the geresh signs alike; a mark is as the ask defines it. c.text, c.before, c.after, c.group and c.container are the template's. Directly before and directly after mean the adjacent character with nothing skipped; skipping whitespace is said where it is meant. A string begins with an entry when its first characters are exactly that entry; no word end is asked unless the words ask it. A word list is compared in lowercase on both sides unless the test says case kept. At the start or the end of a string there is no character, so a test for a character there fails. Literal strings stand in double quotes in these steps; a stop outside the quotes belongs to the sentence.
definitions.first_match: For each mark the shapes are tried in the order they stand in this file, and the first whose test holds names the occurrence; so each test speaks only of occurrences that no shape above it, for the same mark, has taken. A test has no container test unless its words state one; the shape's container field states the container and the checker compares it. No semicolon, colon, exclamation mark or en dash stands in a text whose brackets do not balance, so those marks have no in_unbalanced_text shape.
definitions.top_view: The top view of a string: go through it character by character with a depth that starts at 0. A character "(", "[", "<" or "{" adds one to the depth and is dropped. A character ")", "]", ">" or "}" takes one from the depth if the depth is above 0 and is dropped. Any other character is kept only if the depth is 0.
definitions.list_text: The list text of a string: take its top_view and trim it; if it now ends in ".", remove that one character and trim again.
definitions.pieces: The pieces of a list text: cut it at every "," and every ";" and trim each part. An empty part stays as an empty piece. Positions count from 0, so the first piece is at position 0.
definitions.word: The words of a piece are its maximal runs of non-whitespace characters. A piece is one word when it has exactly one such run. Its first word is compared in lowercase unless a test says case kept.
definitions.plain: A list text is plain when both hold: (1) it holds no Hebrew character; (2) after every occurrence of each string of abbreviations_in_lists is taken out of it, case kept, every mark left in it is "," or ";", or else is "-", "'" or U+2019 with a letter or a digit directly before it and a letter or a digit directly after it.
definitions.opens_with: A string opens with an entry of a list when, in lowercase, it begins with the entry and the character directly after the entry is whitespace. A string that is only the entry does not open with it.
definitions.tail: The tail start of a list of pieces is the position of the first piece, after position 0, that opens_with an entry of tail_openers or that, in lowercase, equals an entry of etc_pieces. If there is no such piece there is no tail. A comma or semicolon is in_tail when the number of commas and semicolons in the top_view of c.before, plus one, is at least the tail start of the pieces of the list_text of the route text.
definitions.named_first: The first piece of a list is named when all of these hold: its first word, case kept, is not exactly "To"; the whole first piece, case kept, is no entry of common_word_heads; and its first word, or, if that word is "a", "an" or "the" and another word follows, its second word, begins with an uppercase letter.
definitions.list_tests: On a list of pieces. one_word_list: every piece is one word. later_capital: some piece after position 0 begins with an uppercase letter and its first word, case kept, is not "I", "A", "An" or "The". to_list: the first word of every piece is "to". to_word_list: the first piece has exactly two words, the first of them "to", and every later piece is one word. article_list: the first word of every piece is "a", "an" or "the", every piece has at most four words, and no word after a piece's first word holds an uppercase letter. article_word_list: the first piece has exactly two words, the first "a", "an" or "the" and the second holding no uppercase letter; later_capital does not hold; every later piece is one word. article_name_list: the first piece has exactly two words, the first "a", "an" or "the" and the second beginning with an uppercase letter; every later piece is one word. word_list: one_word_list, to_list, to_word_list, article_list or article_word_list. own_plural: any two pieces of the list, wherever they stand and in either order, taken in lowercase as a and b, with b equal to a plus "s", or a plus "es", or a ending in "y" and b equal to a without that "y" plus "ies"; or all the pieces in lowercase, joined with ", ", equal an entry of own_plural_texts. small_verb_list: the first piece in lowercase equals an entry of small_verbs or begins with such an entry and a space, and the first word of some later piece is no entry of small_verb_stops. definition_list: the first piece has at most four words, and some later piece has its first word in definition_openers or has five words or more.
definitions.list_kind: The list kind of a route text T, by these steps in order, the first that applies. Each step keeps the subject it states: where a step says T, "begins with" is on T trimmed, case kept; where it says t in lowercase, it is on that string. (1) T begins with an entry of not_list_openings: not_list. (2) T begins with an entry of word_and_definition_openings: definition. Let t be the list_text of T and P its pieces. (3) t holds ":": colon. (4) t holds a Hebrew character: hebrew. (5) t is not plain, or some piece of P is empty: signs. (6) t in lowercase equals an entry of name_labels, or begins with such an entry directly followed by whitespace, "," or ";": name_label. (7) t opens_with an entry of usage_line_openers, by the definition opens_with: usage_line. (8) T begins with an entry of name_description_openings, or the first piece is named_first and the first word of some later piece is an entry of description_openers: name_description. (9) t in lowercase does not begin with an entry of lists_with_an_opener_word and P has a tail: tail. (10) T holds a character of "(", ")", "[", "]": small_verb if P is a small_verb_list, otherwise names if later_capital holds, otherwise bracket. (11) P is own_plural: phrases. (12) P is a one_word_list: names if later_capital holds and t in lowercase is no entry of capital_lists_kept_plain, otherwise one_word. (13) P is a to_list or a to_word_list: verbs. (14) P is an article_list or an article_word_list: articles. (15) P is an article_name_list: names. (16) P is a small_verb_list: small_verb. (17) later_capital holds: names. (18) the first word of the first piece is "to": phrases. (19) P is a definition_list and T does not begin with an entry of plain_list_openings: definition. (20) otherwise: phrases.
definitions.explanation_start: The explanation start of a route text T whose list kind is definition: 1 if T trimmed begins with an entry of word_and_definition_openings, case kept; otherwise the position of the first piece of its list_text, after position 0, whose first word is in definition_openers or that has five words or more; 1 if there is none. The comma or semicolon just before that piece is the one sign between the word and what is said of it.
definitions.small_verb_here: small_verb_here holds of a comma or semicolon when one of these holds. The list_kind of the route text is small_verb. Or it is tail, the mark is not in_tail, and the pieces before the tail start are a small_verb_list. Or it is colon, and by near_colon the side is right, the colon_kind is definition or at_end, the stretch is a list_stretch and its pieces are a small_verb_list.
definitions.capital_head: capital_head holds of a comma when the list_kind of the route text is colon and, by near_colon, the side is right, the colon_kind is definition or at_end, the stretch is a list_stretch, and later_capital holds of its pieces.
definitions.remark_next: remark_next holds of a semicolon when the first piece of the list_text of c.after, in lowercase, equals an entry of tail_openers, or that piece opens_with such an entry.
definitions.colon_kind: The top colons of a text are the colons at depth 0 when it is walked as in top_view; no colon stands in a text whose brackets do not balance, so a colon whose container is top is a top colon. The colon kind of a top colon, by these steps in order, the first that applies. Let L be the top_view of the text before it, trimmed; R the list_text of the text after it. (1) R is empty: at_end. (2) a digit stands directly before the colon and a digit directly after it: reference. (3) R begins with "-" or U+2013 followed by whitespace or by nothing: before_dash. (4) R begins with "the " and holds "letter of the Hebrew alphabet", both case kept: name. Let label mean that L in lowercase begins with an entry of label_openers, an entry's spaces being part of it; let note mean that R opens_with an entry of note_openers. (5) L is label or holds a Hebrew character, and R holds a Hebrew character or is note: between_notes. (6) label: label. (7) L holds a Hebrew character: after_pointer. (8) R holds a Hebrew character: before_pointer. (9) note: before_note. (10) L, case kept, equals an entry of name_heads or begins with an entry of name_head_openings: name. (11) L, case kept, equals an entry of points_back_heads and R holds the word "this" or "these", lowercase, with no letter directly on either side: points_back. (12) otherwise: definition.
definitions.near_colon: For a comma or semicolon at top level. If a top colon stands after the mark: the side is right, the colon is the nearest such one, and the stretch is the list_text of what stands between the nearest top colon before the mark (or the start of the text) and that colon. Otherwise, if a top colon stands before the mark: the side is left, the colon is the nearest one before it, and the stretch is the list_text of all that stands after that colon. The colon_kind named in a test is the kind of that colon.
definitions.list_stretch: A stretch is a list_stretch when it is plain, none of its pieces is empty, and its pieces have no tail.
definitions.marked_place: The lists places_marked_by_hand, note_and_reading_marks, one_word_twice, derived_form_lists, same_head_lists and one_construction_lists hold entries of the same form. Take an entry's pipes out and compare it with the route text, case kept. An entry that begins with U+2026 stands at the end of the text: without that sign it must be the text's last characters. Any other entry stands at the beginning: it must be the text's first characters. A mark that lies in that stretch is marked by the entry when a pipe stands directly after it in the entry, otherwise unmarked by it. Pipes are not in the text. In a test: a mark is a marked place of a list, or a listed_cut, when some entry of the list marks it; a mark is unmarked in a list when some entry of the list covers it and no entry of the list marks it.
definitions.label_word_before: label_word_before holds of a comma when the route text does not begin, case kept, with "Also, ", its list_kind is not one_word, and the part of the top_view of c.before after its last ",", ";" or ":", or the whole top_view if none of the three stands there, trimmed and in lowercase, equals an entry of label_pieces.
definitions.round_kind: The round kind of a round bracket pair, by these steps in order, the first that applies; g is what the pair holds (c.group), b the text before its opener, a the text after its closer. For a closer, b is c.text up to the place c.group and its opener start, and a is c.after. (1) the bracket's container is bracket: in_square. (2) its container is paren: in_round. (3) (a begins with a letter) or (b ends in a letter and g is made only of letters and "-" or is empty): word_part. (4) g holds no letter and no digit: only_signs. (5) the last character of b, skipping whitespace, is a Hebrew character, or b ends in a Hebrew character, one or more whitespace characters, the single lowercase letter "m" or "f" and any whitespace: then, g trimmed begins with """ or U+201C: quoted_after_hebrew; g trimmed begins with "=", or g holds a Hebrew character, or g trimmed in lowercase begins with an entry of notes_after_hebrew, an entry's spaces being part of it: note_after_hebrew; otherwise romanization. (6) g holds a Hebrew character: holds_hebrew. (7) g trimmed in lowercase equals an entry of subject_words: subject. (8) it equals "male" or "female": gender. (9) it equals an entry of conjugation_notes: conjugation. (10) it equals an entry of object_slots: object. (11) b trimmed is empty and a trimmed is not: opens_text. (12) a holds no letter and no digit, and b, with whitespace removed from its end, ends in ".": after_stop. (13) a holds no letter and no digit: ends_text. (14) otherwise: in_text.
definitions.never_opened: A closing bracket never opened when c.group is the empty string and c.before does not end in the matching opening bracket (the ask's step 4). Every closing round bracket that does not meet this has a partner.
definitions.square_kind: The square kind of a square bracket pair, by these steps in order, the first that applies; g is c.group trimmed. Every square bracket in these routes has a partner, so c.group is never null here. (1) the route text holds "[[": link_markup. (2) g begins with "with ", case kept: with. (3) g begins with "see ", case kept: see. (4) g begins with "=": equals. (5) g holds no letter and no digit: only_signs. (6) g holds U+031E: sound. (7) otherwise: supplied.
definitions.pair_follows_hebrew: Walk back through c.before from its end, counting closers against openers of all four bracket kinds, to the opener of the innermost bracket that holds the mark; pair_follows_hebrew holds when the last character before that opener, skipping whitespace, is a Hebrew character.
definitions.run_before: run_before of a string: the longest run at its very end made of letters, digits and "." that ends in a letter or a digit; the empty string if there is none.

branches.question: Some lines are lists of words and phrases with commas or semicolons between them: physical wound, injury, cut. Here the text alone does not show that each piece stands by itself, so the ledger read these lists and kept out those where it found a piece that cannot stand alone. Does each comma or semicolon of these lists divide? A word beside its own plural, such as history, histories, is among them. Many of these lists also say mostly the same thing, and the answer to the question on words that mostly say the same thing does not reach them.

options.means: Each comma or semicolon of these lists cuts: the page prints physical wound, injury and cut as three readings. A small word the source put there, such as or, stays in its piece.
No sign of these cuts: the page prints physical wound, injury, cut as one reading, as written.
